title: Real-Time Card Fraud Detection System (SLA < 100ms)
subtitle: Apache Flink Streaming Windows, Redis Cluster Feature Store & Rule/ML Fallback
problem_statement: Design a real-time anti-fraud payment scoring system processing 10,000 TPS under a strict hard deadline of < 100 milliseconds per transaction (payment network timeout is 200ms). The architecture must evaluate sliding window velocity counters (5m, 24h), user device fingerprint history, deterministic compliance rules (Drools), and machine learning risk scoring (LightGBM/ONNX) with zero downtime.

faded_bug.description: Sequential execution of ML inference without timeout or Circuit Breaker breaches the 100ms payment SLA during upstream traffic spikes.

invariants.description: Scoring engine MUST respond within 95ms under all conditions; fallback to rules is triggered at 60ms.

probing_ladder.stage_1_validation: Explain the architectural trade-off between deterministic rules (Drools) and ML models (LightGBM/ONNX) in financial fraud detection.
probing_ladder.stage_2_tightening: If the payment network timeout is 200ms and downstream bank systems require 100ms, how much budget do you allocate to the ML service? What happens at 61ms?
probing_ladder.stage_3_adversarial: A sophisticated fraudster splits transactions into 10 rapid payments of 999₽ across 10 cards in 3 seconds. How does Apache Flink update the Redis velocity counters in real time?
probing_ladder.stage_4_squeeze: How do you avoid hot-partitioning in Kafka when millions of transactions arrive with the same merchant ID?

counter_probes.counter_question: What happens if the ML service becomes unreachable or takes 500ms during Black Friday? Do you reject payments or let them through?
counter_probes.expected_staff_answer: We enforce a Circuit Breaker with a 60ms hard timeout. If ML degrades, we execute Graceful Fallback to deterministic heuristic rules (whitelist, velocity thresholds) without blocking payments.
